title: PhysisML: a language model trained from scratch on a developmental curriculum, with dream consolidation against catastrophic forgetting
description:
PhysisML (φυσις physis, nature/growth, + ML) is a language model implemented from scratch — a decoder-only transformer with every layer's forward and backward pass hand-written in NumPy, plus a PyTorch mirror for speed — and trained on a developmental curriculum of thirteen Italian levels (phonemes to question answering), with a dynamic vocabulary that grows during training and a rule-based tutor that grades every answer, so the whole curriculum reproduces offline.

Each teaching session ends in a dream: a consolidation pass that replays every previous level's question-answer corpus. The dream is what turns catastrophic forgetting (~20% retention across levels) into ~88%. The repository includes a head-to-head benchmark of the dream against online Elastic Weight Consolidation (Schwarz et al. 2018) on the same harness (exp_i): in this near-perfect-memorization curriculum regime, the implementation of standard online EWC with an empirical diagonal Fisher substantially underperforms experience replay on both seeds (final-row retention 13.0% vs 64.4%), landing below even the no-protection floor (22.0%), because at near-zero training loss the empirical Fisher measures inter-example gradient variance concentrated on shared structural tokens — an anti-selective anchor that freezes the answer-production machinery instead of the knowledge. The comparison is not compute-matched, so the relative efficiency of the two methods remains open.

The repository contains the full training code, the Italian curriculum, the teaching loop with rule-based/local-LLM/API tutors, the retention benchmark harness, and documentation in English and Italian.
